introduction: These readings speak in the language of the Last Day: the trumpet blown, the heaven cleft, the sun folded up, the stars fallen, the mountains moved, the dead raised, the Balance set. They say that all this has happened, in the coming of a new Revelation, and that such words were never meant in their outward sense; and they wonder that people sleep through it. Each of the seventy-six quotations is read here beside one from elsewhere, most of them the older texts whose imagery is being taken up and declared fulfilled: the Qur'an's short chapters of the Hour, Isaiah, Joel, Daniel, the Gospels' discourse on the end, and the Revelation of John, with Donne, Shelley and Yeats. Nine push back or add a side: Aquinas on the literal sense, the promise in Acts of a visible return, the lightning seen from east to west, Peter's scoffers, the Talmud's warning against calculating the end, Amos, and the poets of a darkness without a dawn.
questions: The readings say that the Hour has come and passed, and most did not notice. What kind of event can be the end of a world and yet be missed?
What is gained, and what is lost, when a cleft heaven and a darkened sun are read as the passing of an old order of religion? Consider Aquinas's rule and Origen's question.
Jesus says that the coming of the Son of man will be like lightning seen from east to west, and Acts promises a return 'in like manner'. How do the readings answer those who wait for that?
Amos warns that the day of the Lord is darkness for those who long for it carelessly. Why might the same day be terror to some and joy to others?
Byron and Yeats imagine an ending with no renewal. What in these readings turns upheaval into the opening of a new creation?

outside.why: Isaiah hears a voice crying: prepare ye the way of the Lord; every valley shall be exalted, and every mountain made low.
The letter to the Hebrews quotes the promise: yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven.
The Revelation says: behold, he cometh with clouds, and every eye shall see him.
This is the verse recalled, from the Qur'an: the hour drew nigh and the moon was rent in twain.
A chapter of the Qur'an begins with these words and takes its name from them: when the heaven is cleft asunder.
This is the passage being explained: the trumpet is blown, and all swoon away; then it is blown a second time, and behold them standing waiting.
The Qur'an continues: and the earth shineth with the light of her Lord, and the Book is set up.
Paul writes of a mystery: in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump, the dead shall be raised.
This is the verse of the Revelation being read: after three days and an half the spirit of life from God entered into them.
Ezekiel is set down in a valley full of dry bones, and asked: son of man, can these bones live?
This is the verse of the Revelation being read: a woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet.
John is told to seal up what the seven thunders uttered, and to write them not.
Daniel is told that the words are closed up and sealed till the time of the end.
Paul writes that the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night.
Jesus says that of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven.
Jesus says that as it was in the days of Noah, they ate, they drank, they married, until the flood came.
The Qur'an says that the Hour is surely coming, there is no doubt thereof, yet most of mankind believe not.
Jesus ends his warning with a single word for everyone: what I say unto you I say unto all, Watch.
The Qur'an tells of the earth shaken with her earthquake and yielding up her burdens, while man asks what aileth her.
The Qur'an says of that day, in one of its shortest chapters, that the mountains will become as carded wool.
A chapter of the Qur'an begins with the words that this praise takes up: when the sun is overthrown.
Ezekiel has God say: behold, O my people, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves.
Isaiah says that the desert shall rejoice and blossom as the rose, and that waters shall break out in the wilderness.
Isaiah says that the earth is utterly broken down, and shall reel to and fro like a drunkard.
At the opening of the sixth seal John sees the sun become black as sackcloth, the stars fall, and the heaven depart as a scroll.
Malachi promises: unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings.
The Revelation ends with an invitation: let him that is athirst come, and take the water of life freely.
Joel says that the day of the Lord is great and very terrible, and asks who can abide it.
Donne calls on the angels to blow their trumpets at the round earth's imagined corners, and on the numberless souls to arise from death.
This is the verse the passage echoes: on that day every nursing mother will forget her nursling.
When the seventh angel sounds, great voices in heaven say that the kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord.

Peter's letter expects scoffers who ask where the promise of his coming is, since all things continue as they were. What would those scoffers, and what would the believers, make of the answer 'Nay, it has passed'?
Jesus tells his disciples not to follow those who say, see here, or see there.
Zephaniah says that the great day of the Lord is near, and hasteth greatly.
Jesus says that the hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God.
John sees the dead, small and great, stand before God, and the books opened.
John hears a voice like many waters and mighty thunderings saying: Alleluia, for the Lord God omnipotent reigneth.
The psalm bids the sea roar and the field be joyful, and says that all the trees of the wood shall rejoice before the Lord.
Joel says that the sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great day of the Lord.
Jesus says that the sun shall be darkened, the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven.
Isaiah says that the stars of heaven shall not give their light, and the sun shall be darkened in his going forth.

Amos warns those who long for the day of the Lord that it is darkness, and not light, as if a man fled from a lion and a bear met him. Why is the Hour a terror to some and the fulfilment of hope to others?
Haggai has God say: I will shake the heavens, and the earth, and the sea, and I will shake all nations.
Daniel reads a king his sentence: thou art weighed in the balances, and art found wanting.
Another chapter of the Qur'an opens with the same sign and takes its name from it: when the heaven is split asunder.
Isaiah says that the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens rolled together as a scroll.
Origen asked who of understanding will suppose that the first days of creation, with evening and morning, existed without a sun.
Maimonides read Isaiah's wolf dwelling with the lamb as a metaphor and a parable.

Aquinas held that all the senses of scripture are founded on the literal, from which alone can any argument be drawn. If cleft heavens and fallen stars are figures, what in these verses can still be argued from?
The Qur'an speaks of the day when the heavens are rolled up as a recorder rolleth up a written scroll.
John sees a great white throne, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away.
Peter tells the crowd at Pentecost that what they see is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel of the last days.
Jesus speaks of signs in the sun and moon, distress of nations with perplexity, and men's hearts failing them for fear.
Isaiah prays: oh that thou wouldest rend the heavens, that thou wouldest come down, that the mountains might flow down at thy presence.
Daniel sees in the night visions one like the Son of man come with the clouds of heaven.

In Acts the disciples watch Jesus taken up, and are told that he shall so come in like manner as they have seen him go. How should those who wait for a figure in the sky hear the announcement that he has come riding upon the clouds?
Isaiah has God say: behold, I create new heavens and a new earth, and the former shall not be remembered.
The Talmud curses those who calculate the end of days, because when the date passes people say that the Messiah will never come. What is the right use of prophecies about signs and times?
Jesus ends many of his sayings with the words: he that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
Daniel says that many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake.
Isaiah is sent to a people who hear indeed but understand not, and see indeed but perceive not.
John's Gospel says that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light.

Jesus says that the coming of the Son of man will be as the lightning that cometh out of the east and shineth even unto the west. If the Call is as plain as that, how can a whole people fail to perceive it?
The Qur'an says that their reckoning draweth nigh for mankind, while they turn away in heedlessness.
Matthew says that at the death of Jesus the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom.
Jesus says that faith as a grain of mustard seed shall say to a mountain, remove hence, and it shall remove.
Yeats wrote in 1919 that things fall apart, the centre cannot hold, and mere anarchy is loosed upon the world.
John sees a new heaven and a new earth, for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away.
The Qur'an speaks of the day when the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens also.
Peter's letter says that the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat.
Peter's letter adds that we look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness.

Hardy, at the end of a dying century, hears an aged thrush fling its soul upon the gloom, and thinks that it knows of some blessed hope of which he is unaware. What is it to hear a call that others around you do not?
Jesus says: ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars; see that ye be not troubled, for the end is not yet.
Yeats, after a great war, asks what rough beast, its hour come round at last, slouches towards Bethlehem to be born. Why does carnage lead him to dread and this reading to the hope of justice?
Shelley sings that the world's great age begins anew, and the earth renews her winter weeds outworn.
Byron dreamed that the bright sun was extinguished, and the icy earth swung blind in the moonless air; in his poem no dawn follows. What makes the darkened sun of these readings good news?

revelation-sun-black-as-sackcloth.text: And I beheld when he had opened the sixth seal, and, lo, there was a great earthquake; and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the moon became as blood; And the stars of heaven fell unto the earth, even as a fig tree casteth her untimely figs, when she is shaken of a mighty wind. isaiah-heavens-rolled-together.text: And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree

joel-sun-into-darkness.text: And I will shew wonders in the heavens and in the earth, blood, and fire, and pillars of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and terrible day of the Lord come

hebrews-yet-once-more-i-shake.text: Whose voice then shook the earth: but now he hath promised, saying, Yet once more I shake not the earth only, but also heaven. And this word, Yet once more, signifieth the removing of those things that are shaken, as of things that are made, that those things which cannot be shaken may remain

revelation-seventh-angel-sounded.text: And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever

isaiah-stars-shall-not-give-their-light.text: Behold, the day of the Lord cometh, cruel both with wrath and fierce anger, to lay the land desolate: and he shall destroy the sinners thereof out of it. For the stars of heaven and the constellations thereof shall not give their light: the sun shall be darkened in his going forth, and the moon shall not cause her light to shine

revelation-spirit-of-life-entered.text: And after three days and an half the spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them

ezekiel-dry-bones.text: The hand of the Lord was upon me, and carried me out in the spirit of the Lord, and set me down in the midst of the valley which was full of bones, And caused me to pass by them round about: and, behold, there were very many in the open valley; and, lo, they were very dry. And he said unto me, Son of man, can these bones live? And I answered, O Lord God, thou knowest

revelation-first-earth-passed-away-sea.text: And I saw a great white throne, and him that sat on it, from whose face the earth and the heaven fled away; and there was found no place for them

matthew-of-that-day-knoweth-no-man.text: But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only

luke-not-with-observation-lo-here.text: And he said unto the disciples, The days will come, when ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, and ye shall not see it. And they shall say to you, See here; or, see there: go not after them, nor follow them. For as the lightning, that lighteneth out of the one part under heaven, shineth unto the other part under heaven; so shall also the Son of man be in his day

donne-round-earths-imagined-corners.text: At the round earth's imagined corners blow / Your trumpets, angels, and arise, arise / From death, you numberless infinities / Of souls, and to your scattered bodies go
donne-round-earths-imagined-corners.author: John Donne

byron-bright-sun-was-extinguished.text: I had a dream, which was not all a dream. / The bright sun was extinguished, and the stars / Did wander darkling in the eternal space, / Rayless, and pathless, and the icy Earth / Swung blind and blackening in the moonless air
byron-bright-sun-was-extinguished.author: Lord Byron
